implement_reported: The fix pass (d153126) added a refusal the design does not name: a ./warden.toml that is not a regular file once links are followed is an error, while a file named by --config or WARDEN_CONFIG is read whatever kind it is. Judged as finding 1.

findings.also: GLOBAL-09 (SHOULD): the default 'the working directory's warden.toml, if it exists' gains a condition the Defaults and overrides section does not list
findings.what: readConfigFile refuses a ./warden.toml found in the working directory that is not a regular file once links are followed (a link to /dev/zero, a terminal, a FIFO), with 'cannot read config file ... (found in the working directory): not a regular file'. The design approved at a94133d does not decide this. Its lookup (How the config file is found) is './warden.toml exists -> it', and the only errors for that file are a stat failure other than 'does not exist' and a file that cannot be read; a device or FIFO can be read. Its Defaults and overrides row for the default file has no such condition. Its Security note item 10 weighs the same hazard (a FIFO nobody writes to, an endless device, chosen by the repository through its warden.toml) for CA paths and leaves it as on main; the config file itself being such a file is not discussed. On main such a ./warden.toml is read (and hangs or exhausts memory). The behaviour is reasonable, conservative, documented in the reference and tested, but it is a design decision made in code: FLOW-06 asks for it to go back to Design, and code alone does not name a change to a default.
findings.fix: back-to-design (FLOW-06), recommended: Design adds the condition to the default's row in Defaults and overrides (and the asymmetry: a named file is read whatever kind it is), the error to 'How the config file is found', and one sentence to Security note item 10; a delta review approves it, and the code stays as it is. Alternative with no return to Design: remove the errNotRegular case and its reference text and test, so ./warden.toml is read whatever kind it is, as the approved design and main have it.

findings.lines: driver/session.go (LoadUpstreamCAs, scanCAFile, ClaimRelay); driver/hostutil.go:126 (ModuleRoot); cmd/warden/config.go:138 (configFile); driver/driver.go:83
findings.what: The change alters trust-root handling across the host-relay boundary (only valid PEM certificates, re-encoded, are sent in the claim; paths are read once, before anything is created; the claim opens no file), removes the user-level config file, and stops ModuleRoot from treating the working directory's go.mod as warden's source tree (a host code-execution path). This is a security-boundary change by GLOBAL-06's definition. The design carries the Security note the rule asks for (accepted at r1) and says TEST-08 runs; its four corpus entries are handed to security-suite at Publish (task 26).
findings.fix: Nothing to change in the code. The human acknowledges at merge with the Security note in the PR body, and TEST-08's adversarial arm runs before the release that carries this (the design says the change trips it).
